8. Post-condition: the condition that the system and the output must satisfy after the operation is executed.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

```plantuml
@startuml

title arborparser Model

class AutoPruneStrategy {
    addNodeAndUpdateBranch(node : ChainNode, currentBranch : List<TreeNode>) : void
    addNodeToTree(node : ChainNode, currentBranch : List<TreeNode>, currentNodeRef : node) : void
    buildTree(chain : List<ChainNode>) : TreeNode
    createTreeNode(chainnode : ChainNode) : TreeNode
    isAllNotImmNodesSiblings(queue : Deque) : void
}
class BaseNode {
    content : String
    levelSeq : List<int>
    levelText : String
    title : String
    concatNode(node : BaseNode) : void
}
class ChainNode {
    patternPriority : int
}
class ChainParser {
    patterns : List<LevelPattern>
    createChainNode(levelSeq : List<int>, title : String, content : String, levelText : String, patternPriority : int) : ChainNode
    detectLevel(line : String) : ChainNode
    parseToChain(text : String) : List<ChainNode>
}
class LevelPattern {
    description : String
    failOnConvert : boolean
    fixedLevelSeq : List<EIntegerObject>
    maxLevel : int
    minLevel : int
    numberType : NumberType
    regexText : String
    separator : String
    helper : ParserHelper
    convertMatchedText(matchedText : String) : List<EIntegerObject>
    getRegex() : Pattern
}
class ParserHelper {
    convertNumber(numberType : NumberType, text : String) : EIntegerObject
    getNumberPattern(numberType : NumberType) : String
}
class PatternBuilder {
    maxLevel : int
    minLevel : int
    numberType : NumberType
    prefixRegex : String
    separator : String
    suffixRegex : String
    build() : LevelPattern
    copySelf() : PatternBuilder
    modify(newPrefixRegex : String, newMinLevel : int) : PatternBuilder
    validate() : void
}
class StrictStrategy {
    buildTree(chain : List<ChainNode>) : TreeNode
    createTreeNode(chainnode : ChainNode) : TreeNode
    isChild(parentSeq : List<EIntegerObject>, childSeq : List<EIntegerObject>) : boolean
}
class TreeBuilder {
    strategy : TreeBuildingStrategy
    buildTree(chain : List<ChainNode>) : TreeNode
}
abstract class TreeBuildingStrategy {
    buildTree(chain : List<ChainNode>) : TreeNode
    getLastLevel(levelSeq : List<EIntegerObject>) : int
    getPrefix(levelSeq : List<EIntegerObject>) : List<EIntegerObject>
    isImmNext(frontSeq : List<EIntegerObject>, backSeq : List<EIntegerObject>) : boolean
    isRoot(node : BaseNode) : boolean
}
class TreeExporter {
    escapeJson(s : String) : String
    exportChain(chain : List<ChainNode>) : String
    exportToJson(tree : TreeNode) : String
    exportToJsonFile(tree : TreeNode, filePath : Path) : void
    exportTree(tree : TreeNode) : String
    exportTreeInternal(node : TreeNode, prefix : String, isLast : boolean, isRoot : boolean) : String
    nodeToDict(node : TreeNode) : EMap
    toJson(obj : EJavaObject, indent : int) : String
}
class TreeNode {
    children : List<TreeNode>
    parent : TreeNode
    addChild(child : TreeNode) : void
    getFullContent() : String
    mergeAllChildren() : void
}
enum NumberType {
    ARABIC
    ROMAN
    CHINESE
    LETTER
    CIRCLED
}

AutoPruneStrategy --|> TreeBuildingStrategy
ChainNode --|> BaseNode
ChainParser *-- "*" LevelPattern : patterns
LevelPattern --> ParserHelper : helper
StrictStrategy --|> TreeBuildingStrategy
TreeBuilder --> TreeBuildingStrategy : strategy
TreeNode --|> BaseNode
TreeNode *-- "*" TreeNode : children  'opposite: parent
TreeNode --> TreeNode : parent  'opposite: children
@enduml
```

```plantuml
abstract class TreeBuildingStrategy {
    buildTree(chain : List<ChainNode>) : TreeNode
    getLastLevel(levelSeq : List<EIntegerObject>) : int
    getPrefix(levelSeq : List<EIntegerObject>) : List<EIntegerObject>
    isImmNext(frontSeq : List<EIntegerObject>, backSeq : List<EIntegerObject>) : boolean
    isRoot(node : BaseNode) : boolean
}
class TreeExporter {
    escapeJson(s : String) : String
    exportChain(chain : List<ChainNode>) : String
    exportToJson(tree : TreeNode) : String
    exportToJsonFile(tree : TreeNode, filePath : Path) : void
    exportTree(tree : TreeNode) : String
    exportTreeInternal(node : TreeNode, prefix : String, isLast : boolean, isRoot : boolean) : String
    nodeToDict(node : TreeNode) : EMap
    toJson(obj : EJavaObject, indent : int) : String
}
class TreeNode {
    children : List<TreeNode>
    parent : TreeNode
    addChild(child : TreeNode) : void
    getFullContent() : String
    mergeAllChildren() : void
}
enum NumberType {
    ARABIC
    ROMAN
    CHINESE
    LETTER
    CIRCLED
}

AutoPruneStrategy --|> TreeBuildingStrategy
ChainNode --|> BaseNode
ChainParser *-- "*" LevelPattern : patterns
LevelPattern --> ParserHelper : helper
StrictStrategy --|> TreeBuildingStrategy
TreeBuilder --> TreeBuildingStrategy : strategy
TreeNode --|> BaseNode
TreeNode *-- "*" TreeNode : children  'opposite: parent
TreeNode --> TreeNode : parent  'opposite: children
@enduml
```

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

# Operation Specifications
TreeBuildingStrategy::getPrefix
Summary:
Returns the level sequence without its last component, i.e., the parent sequence.
Algorithm:
1. If levelSeq is null, return an empty list.
2. If levelSeq.size() <= 1, return an empty list.
3. Return a new list containing levelSeq[0 ... size-2].
Related Features: getLastLevel, isImmNext
Related Classes: None
Input: levelSeq - list of integer levels.
Output: List of integer levels representing the parent sequence.
Pre-condition: levelSeq is not null.
Post-condition: The returned list is the prefix of levelSeq without the last element.

TreeBuildingStrategy::getLastLevel
Summary:
Returns the last integer in a level sequence, used to compare sibling order.
Algorithm:
1. If levelSeq is null or empty, return 0 (or a neutral sentinel).
2. Return the last element of levelSeq.
Related Features: None
Related Classes: None
Input: levelSeq - list of integer levels.
Output: int value of the last level component.
Pre-condition: levelSeq is not null; for empty sequences the sentinel 0 is returned.
Post-condition: The output is the numeric value of the final sequence element.

TreeBuildingStrategy::isRoot
Summary:
Tests whether a node is the synthetic root node.
Algorithm:
1. If node is null, return false.
2. Return node.levelSeq is null or empty.
Related Features: levelSeq
Related Classes: TreeBuildingStrategy, BaseNode
Input: node - BaseNode (or TreeNode) to test.
Output: boolean true if the node has an empty level sequence.
Pre-condition: node is not null.
Post-condition: The root node is identified by its empty level sequence.

```text
Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. # Operation Specifications
```
TreeBuildingStrategy::getPrefix
Summary:
Returns the level sequence without its last component, i.e., the parent sequence.
Algorithm:
1. If levelSeq is null, return an empty list.
2. If levelSeq.size() <= 1, return an empty list.
3. Return a new list containing levelSeq[0 ... size-2].
Related Features: getLastLevel, isImmNext
Related Classes: None
Input: levelSeq - list of integer levels.
Output: List of integer levels representing the parent sequence.
Pre-condition: levelSeq is not null.
Post-condition: The returned list is the prefix of levelSeq without the last element.

TreeBuildingStrategy::getLastLevel
Summary:
Returns the last integer in a level sequence, used to compare sibling order.
Algorithm:
1. If levelSeq is null or empty, return 0 (or a neutral sentinel).
2. Return the last element of levelSeq.
Related Features: None
Related Classes: None
Input: levelSeq - list of integer levels.
Output: int value of the last level component.
Pre-condition: levelSeq is not null; for empty sequences the sentinel 0 is returned.
Post-condition: The output is the numeric value of the final sequence element.

TreeBuildingStrategy::isRoot
Summary:
Tests whether a node is the synthetic root node.
Algorithm:
1. If node is null, return false.
2. Return node.levelSeq is null or empty.
Related Features: levelSeq
Related Classes: TreeBuildingStrategy, BaseNode
Input: node - BaseNode (or TreeNode) to test.
Output: boolean true if the node has an empty level sequence.
Pre-condition: node is not null.
Post-condition: The root node is identified by its empty level sequence.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

# Operation Specifications
PatternBuilder::validate
Summary:
Validates the builder state before it is used to build a LevelPattern. If the state is invalid, the operation fails.
Algorithm:
1. Check prefixRegex, separator, suffixRegex are non-null.
2. Check numberType is non-null.
3. Check minLevel >= 0.
4. Check maxLevel >= minLevel.
5. Try to compile the composed regular expression; if compilation fails, reject.
6. If all checks pass, return normally.
Related Features: prefixRegex, separator, suffixRegex, numberType, minLevel, maxLevel
Related Classes: PatternBuilder, NumberType
Input: None.
Output: None; may throw an exception if validation fails.
Pre-condition: Builder fields are in their intended state.
Post-condition: If valid, the builder is ready for build(); if invalid, no LevelPattern is produced.

PatternBuilder::copySelf
Summary:
Creates a copy of this PatternBuilder, preserving all fields.
Algorithm:
1. Create a new PatternBuilder.
2. Copy maxLevel, minLevel, numberType, prefixRegex, separator, suffixRegex.
3. Return the copy.
Related Features: maxLevel, minLevel, numberType, prefixRegex, separator, suffixRegex
Related Classes: PatternBuilder, NumberType
Input: None.
Output: PatternBuilder copy with identical field values.
Pre-condition: this builder is initialized.
Post-condition: Original builder is unchanged; returned builder is independent.

PatternBuilder::modify
Summary:
Returns a modified copy of this builder with a new prefix regex and a new minimum level. The original builder remains unchanged.
Algorithm:
1. Copy this builder using copySelf().
2. Set copy.prefixRegex = newPrefixRegex.
3. Set copy.minLevel = newMinLevel.
4. Return copy.
Related Features: copySelf, prefixRegex, minLevel
Related Classes: PatternBuilder
Input: newPrefixRegex - new regular-expression prefix for the pattern; newMinLevel - minimum allowed level-sequence length.
Output: A new PatternBuilder with the updated fields.
Pre-condition: newPrefixRegex is a valid regular expression; newMinLevel is non-negative and no greater than maxLevel.
Post-condition: The returned builder has the requested prefix and minimum level; the original builder is unchanged.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

# Operation Specifications
StrictStrategy::isChild
Summary:
Tests whether childSeq is a direct child sequence of parentSeq, i.e., childSeq has exactly one more level than parentSeq and parentSeq is its prefix.
Algorithm:
1. If parentSeq or childSeq is null, return false.
2. If childSeq.size() != parentSeq.size() + 1, return false.
3. Return childSeq.subList(0, parentSeq.size()).equals(parentSeq).
Related Features: getPrefix, getLastLevel
Related Classes: StrictStrategy, TreeBuildingStrategy
Input: parentSeq - base level sequence; childSeq - candidate child level sequence.
Output: boolean true if childSeq extends parentSeq by one element; false otherwise.
Pre-condition: parentSeq and childSeq are non-null.
Post-condition: Returns true only when the child relation holds.

StrictStrategy::buildTree
Summary:
Builds a strict outline tree from the parsed chain. Any chain that does not follow the exact immediate level-sequence relation is rejected.
Algorithm:
1. If chain is null or empty, return a synthetic root TreeNode with title "ROOT".
2. If chain[0] is a synthetic root ChainNode (levelSeq empty and title "ROOT"), use it as root and start at index 1.
3. Otherwise create a synthetic root TreeNode.
4. Initialize stack = [root].
5. For each ChainNode cn in the remaining chain:
   a. If stack is empty or not isImmNext(stack.last.levelSeq, cn.levelSeq), reject the chain by raising a construction exception.
   b. While not isChild(stack.last.levelSeq, cn.levelSeq), pop the stack.
   c. Create tn = createTreeNode(cn).
   d. stack.last.addChild(tn).
   e. Push tn onto stack.
6. Return root.
Related Features: isImmNext, isChild, createTreeNode, stack, TreeNode.addChild
Related Classes: StrictStrategy, ChainNode, TreeNode, TreeBuildingStrategy
Input: chain - ordered list of parsed ChainNodes.
Output: TreeNode root of the strictly built outline.
Pre-condition: chain is not null.
Post-condition: If valid, the returned tree follows the exact parent-child and sibling order. If invalid, the chain is rejected (a construction exception is raised and no partial tree is returned).

StrictStrategy::createTreeNode
Summary:
Converts a ChainNode into a TreeNode, copying title, level sequence, level text, and content, and initializing children and parent.
Algorithm:
1. Create a new TreeNode.
2. Copy chainnode.title, chainnode.levelSeq, chainnode.levelText, chainnode.content.
3. Set parent = null.
4. Set children = new empty list.
5. Return tn.
Related Features: ChainNode.title, ChainNode.levelSeq, ChainNode.levelText, ChainNode.content
Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeNode
Input: chainnode - ChainNode to convert.
Output: New TreeNode instance.
Pre-condition: chainnode is not null.
Post-condition: The new TreeNode has the same heading data and no children.

   a. If stack is empty or not isImmNext(stack.last.levelSeq, cn.levelSeq), reject the chain by raising a construction exception.
   b. While not isChild(stack.last.levelSeq, cn.levelSeq), pop the stack.
   c. Create tn = createTreeNode(cn).
   d. stack.last.addChild(tn).
   e. Push tn onto stack.
5. Return root.
Related Features: isImmNext, isChild, createTreeNode, TreeNode.levelSeq, ChainNode.levelSeq, TreeNode.addChild, TreeNode.title
Related Classes: StrictStrategy, ChainNode, TreeNode, TreeBuildingStrategy
Input: chain - ordered list of parsed ChainNodes.
Output: TreeNode root of the strictly built outline.
Pre-condition: chain is not null.
Post-condition: If valid, the returned tree follows the exact parent-child and sibling order. If invalid, the chain is rejected (a construction exception is raised and no partial tree is returned).}

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

# Operation Specifications
ChainParser::detectLevel
Summary:
Tries each registered LevelPattern in order until a valid heading pattern is found. If a pattern matches and numeric conversion succeeds, returns a ChainNode representing the heading; otherwise returns null.
Algorithm:
1. For each pattern p in patterns:
   a. Get matcher = p.getRegex().matcher(line).
   b. If no anchored match, continue to the next pattern.
   c. Extract matchedText from the capturing group that holds the numbering text.
   d. Convert matchedText via p.convertMatchedText(matchedText).
   e. If conversion fails or yields an empty levelSeq:
        if p.failOnConvert or p.fixedLevelSeq is empty, continue to next pattern.
        else use p.fixedLevelSeq as the levelSeq.
   f. If levelSeq.size() < p.minLevel or levelSeq.size() > p.maxLevel, continue.
   g. Determine title = line substring after the matched heading marker and separator, trimmed of leading/trailing whitespace.
   h. Return createChainNode(levelSeq, title, "", matchedText, index of p).
2. If no pattern succeeds, return null.
Related Features: patterns, createChainNode, LevelPattern.getRegex, LevelPattern.convertMatchedText, LevelPattern.failOnConvert, LevelPattern.fixedLevelSeq, LevelPattern.minLevel, LevelPattern.maxLevel
Related Classes: ChainParser, LevelPattern, ChainNode, ParserHelper, NumberType
Input: line - a single input line to test for a heading.
Output: ChainNode if the line is a heading; null otherwise.
Pre-condition: line is not null.
Post-condition: The first valid pattern determines the level sequence and patternPriority; non-heading lines return null.

ChainParser::parseToChain
Summary:
Parses an entire structured text into an ordered list of ChainNodes. Heading lines become ChainNodes; ordinary lines are appended as content to the current section. A synthetic root ChainNode is included when preamble content exists or when no heading is found.
Algorithm:
1. Split text into lines, preserving original line terminators.
2. Initialize result = empty list; current = null; pendingContent = empty.
3. For each line:
   a. cn = detectLevel(line).
   b. If cn != null:
        If current == null and pendingContent is not empty:
            Create a synthetic root ChainNode with levelSeq=[], title="ROOT", content=pendingContent, levelText="", patternPriority=-1, and add it to result.
        Add cn to result.
        current = cn.
        pendingContent = "".
   c. Else:
        If current != null:
            Append the original line to current.content.
        Else:
            Append the original line to pendingContent.
4. After all lines:
   a. If result is empty:
        Create a synthetic root ChainNode with content=pendingContent and add it to result.
   b. Else if pendingContent is not empty:
        Create a synthetic root ChainNode with content=pendingContent and insert it at the beginning of result.
5. Return result.
Related Features: detectLevel, createChainNode, current content, pendingContent
Related Classes: ChainParser, ChainNode, BaseNode
Input: text - the plain structured text to parse.
Output: List<ChainNode> in document order; an empty or heading-free text yields a single synthetic root ChainNode.
Pre-condition: text is not null.
Post-condition: Every parsed heading is a ChainNode; all ordinary text lines are preserved as content in the current section or root.

ChainParser::createChainNode
Summary:
Factory method that creates a ChainNode with the given level sequence, title, content, level text, and pattern priority.
Algorithm:
1. Create a new ChainNode.
2. Set cn.levelSeq = levelSeq.
3. Set cn.title = title.
4. Set cn.content = content.
5. Set cn.levelText = levelText.
6. Set cn.patternPriority = patternPriority.
7. Return cn.
Related Features: levelSeq, title, content, levelText, patternPriority
Related Classes: ChainNode, BaseNode
Input: levelSeq - list of integer levels; title - heading title; content - section content; levelText - original matched numbering text; patternPriority - order index of the matched pattern.
Output: ChainNode with the provided values.
Pre-condition: levelSeq, title, content, levelText are non-null; levelSeq may be empty for a synthetic root node.
Post-condition: A new ChainNode is returned with the given properties.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

# Operation Specifications
ChainParser::detectLevel
Summary:
Tries each registered LevelPattern in order until a valid heading pattern is found. If a pattern matches and numeric conversion succeeds, returns a ChainNode representing the heading; otherwise returns null.
Algorithm:
1. For each pattern p in patterns:
   a. Get matcher = p.getRegex().matcher(line).
   b. If no anchored match, continue to the next pattern.
   c. Extract matchedText from the capturing group that holds the numbering text.
   d. Convert matchedText via p.convertMatchedText(matchedText).
   e. If conversion fails or yields an empty levelSeq:
        if p.failOnConvert or p.fixedLevelSeq is empty, continue to next pattern.
        else use p.fixedLevelSeq as the levelSeq.
   f. If levelSeq.size() < p.minLevel or levelSeq.size() > p.maxLevel, continue.
   g. Determine title = line substring after the matched heading marker and separator, trimmed of leading/trailing whitespace.
   h. Return createChainNode(levelSeq, title, "", matchedText, index of p).
2. If no pattern succeeds, return null.
Related Features: patterns, createChainNode, LevelPattern.getRegex, LevelPattern.convertMatchedText, LevelPattern.failOnConvert, LevelPattern.fixedLevelSeq, LevelPattern.minLevel, LevelPattern.maxLevel
Related Classes: ChainParser, LevelPattern, ChainNode, ParserHelper, NumberType
Input: line - a single input line to test for a heading.
Output: ChainNode if the line is a heading; null otherwise.
Pre-condition: line is not null.
Post-condition: The first valid pattern determines the level sequence and patternPriority; non-heading lines return null.

ChainParser::parseToChain
Summary:
Parses an entire structured text into an ordered list of ChainNodes. Heading lines become ChainNodes; ordinary lines are appended as content to the current section. A synthetic root ChainNode is included when preamble content exists or when no heading is found.
Algorithm:

2. Initialize result = empty list; current = null; pendingContent = empty.

        Else:

   b. Else if pendingContent is not empty:

# Operation Specifications
LevelPattern::getRegex
Summary:
Returns the compiled regular expression Pattern for this level pattern. The pattern is compiled lazily and cached.
Algorithm:
1. If the cached Pattern is already available, return it.
2. Compile regexText into a Pattern.
3. Store the compiled Pattern in a private cache.
4. Return the compiled Pattern.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

# Operation Specifications
TreeExporter::exportTreeInternal
Summary:
Recursive helper for exportTree. Formats a node and its children using prefix, last-child flags, and root flags.
Algorithm:
1. If isRoot:
     line = node.title
     childPrefix = ""
   Else:
     line = prefix + (isLast ? "└── " : "├── ") + node.title
     childPrefix = prefix + (isLast ? "    " : "│   ")
2. Append line and a newline.
3. For each child in node.children:
     exportTreeInternal(child, childPrefix, isLast = (child is the last child), isRoot = false).
Related Features: title, children
Related Classes: TreeExporter, TreeNode
Input: node - TreeNode to format; prefix - current indentation/branch prefix; isLast - whether this node is the last child of its parent; isRoot - whether this is the root node.
Output: String containing the node and its subtree in ASCII tree form.
Pre-condition: node is not null; children list is ordered.
Post-condition: The returned string represents the subtree in a stable visual tree.

TreeExporter::nodeToDict
Summary:
Converts a TreeNode into an order-preserving map suitable for JSON serialization.
Algorithm:
1. dict = new EMap().
2. dict["title"] = node.title.
3. dict["level_seq"] = node.levelSeq.
4. dict["level_text"] = node.levelText.
5. dict["content"] = node.content.
6. children = new list.
7. For each child in node.children:
     children.add(nodeToDict(child)).
8. dict["children"] = children.
9. Return dict.
Related Features: title, levelSeq, levelText, content, children
Related Classes: TreeExporter, TreeNode, EMap
Input: node - TreeNode to convert.
Output: EMap with the required JSON field names and values.
Pre-condition: node is not null; children list is ordered.
Post-condition: The returned map preserves child order and contains only the specified fields.

TreeExporter::exportToJsonFile
Summary:
Writes the JSON representation of a tree to the given file path.
Algorithm:
1. json = exportToJson(tree).
2. Open filePath for writing.
3. Write json to the file.
4. Close the file.
Related Features: exportToJson
Related Classes: TreeExporter, TreeNode, Path
Input: tree - TreeNode to write; filePath - destination file path.
Output: None; a file is created or overwritten.
Pre-condition: tree is not null; filePath is writable.
Post-condition: The file contains the same JSON string as exportToJson(tree).

TreeExporter::exportTree
Summary:
Returns a human-readable ASCII tree representation of the TreeNode hierarchy.
Algorithm:
1. If tree is null, return empty string.
2. Return exportTreeInternal(tree, "", true, true).
Related Features: exportTreeInternal
Related Classes: TreeExporter, TreeNode
Input: tree - root TreeNode.
Output: String with tree-drawing branch characters.
Pre-condition: tree is not null.
Post-condition: The output presents the title hierarchy in a deterministic textual tree.

# Operation Specifications
TreeExporter::exportTreeInternal
Summary:
Recursive helper for exportTree. Formats a node and its children using prefix, last-child flags, and root flags.
Algorithm:
1. If isRoot:
     line = node.title
     childPrefix = ""
   Else:
     line = prefix + (isLast ? "└── " : "├── ") + node.title
     childPrefix = prefix + (isLast ? "    " : "│   ")
2. Append line and a newline.
3. For each child in node.children:
     exportTreeInternal(child, childPrefix, isLast = (child is the last child), isRoot = false).
Related Features: title, children
Related Classes: TreeExporter, TreeNode
Input: node - TreeNode to format; prefix - current indentation/branch prefix; isLast - whether this node is the last child of its parent; isRoot - whether this is the root node.
Output: String containing the node and its subtree in ASCII tree form.
Pre-condition: node is not null; children list is ordered.
Post-condition: The returned string represents the subtree in a stable visual tree.

TreeExporter::nodeToDict
Summary:
Converts a TreeNode into an order-preserving map suitable for JSON serialization.
Algorithm:
1. dict = new EMap().
2. dict["title"] = node.title.
3. dict["level_seq"] = node.levelSeq.
4. dict["level_text"] = node.levelText.
5. dict["content"] = node.content.
6. children = new list.
7. For each child in node.children:
     children.add(nodeToDict(child)).
8. dict["children"] = children.
9. Return dict.
Related Features: title, levelSeq, levelText, content, children
Related Classes: TreeExporter, TreeNode, EMap
Input: node - TreeNode to convert.
Output: EMap with the required JSON field names and values.
Pre-condition: node is not null; children list is ordered.
Post-condition: The returned map preserves child order and contains only the specified fields.

TreeExporter::exportToJsonFile

Writes the JSON representation of a tree to the given file path.
Algorithm:
1. json = exportToJson(tree).
2. Open filePath for writing.
3. Write json to the file.
4. Close the file.
Related Features: exportToJson
Related Classes: TreeExporter, TreeNode, Path
Input: tree - TreeNode to write; filePath - destination file path.
Output: None; a file is created or overwritten.
Pre-condition: tree is not null; filePath is writable.
Post-condition: The file contains the same JSON string as exportToJson(tree).

TreeExporter::exportTree

Algorithm:

2. Return exportTreeInternal(tree, "", true, true).
Related Features: exportTreeInternal
Related Classes: TreeExporter, TreeNode
Input: tree - root TreeNode.
Output: String with tree-drawing branch characters.
Pre-condition: tree is not null.
Post-condition: The output presents the title hierarchy in a deterministic textual tree.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

# Operation Specifications
AutoPruneStrategy::addNodeToTree
Summary:
Lower-level helper that creates a TreeNode from a ChainNode, attaches it to the correct ancestor in currentBranch, and updates the current-node reference. It does not automatically append the new node to currentBranch; the caller does that after the branch has been trimmed.
Algorithm:
1. tn = createTreeNode(node)
2. While currentBranch is not empty and not isChild(currentBranch.last.levelSeq, node.levelSeq):
     currentBranch.removeLast()
3. If currentBranch is empty, reject the attachment.
4. parent = currentBranch.last
5. parent.addChild(tn)
6. Set currentNodeRef.value = tn
Related Features: createTreeNode, isChild, currentBranch, TreeNode.addChild
Related Classes: AutoPruneStrategy, ChainNode, TreeNode, TreeBuildingStrategy
Input: node - ChainNode to attach; currentBranch - mutable branch list for finding the parent; currentNodeRef - a mutable reference holder for the newly created current TreeNode.
Output: None; currentBranch and currentNodeRef are updated as side effects.
Pre-condition: node must have an ancestor represented in currentBranch; currentNodeRef is a mutable holder that can receive the new node.
Post-condition: node is linked into the tree under the nearest ancestor, and currentNodeRef refers to the newly added TreeNode.

AutoPruneStrategy::buildTree
Summary:
Builds a tree from the parsed chain using the auto-prune strategy, maintaining the latest valid branch and a pending queue for non-immediate nodes.
Algorithm:
1. Prepare a synthetic root TreeNode with levelSeq=[], title="ROOT", levelText="", content="".
   If the chain starts with a synthetic root ChainNode, use that node as the root and skip it.
2. currentBranch = [root]; current = root; pending = new Deque().
3. For each ChainNode cn in the remaining chain:
   a. If isImmNext(currentBranch.last.levelSeq, cn.levelSeq):
      - Merge every pending node into current.content in arrival order using concatNode.
      - Call addNodeAndUpdateBranch(cn, currentBranch).
      - current = currentBranch.last.
   b. Else:
      - Add cn to pending.
      - If pending.size() >= 3:
         oldSize = pending.size();
         isAllNotImmNodesSiblings(pending);
         if pending.size() == oldSize:
            // All pending nodes are an immediate sibling sequence; attach them in order.
            while pending not empty:
               addNodeAndUpdateBranch(pending.pollFirst(), currentBranch)
            current = currentBranch.last
         else:
            // The oldest pending node was already merged into current.content.
4. After the loop, merge all remaining pending nodes into current.content in arrival order.
5. Return root.
Related Features: isImmNext, addNodeAndUpdateBranch, isAllNotImmNodesSiblings, concatNode, createTreeNode, currentBranch, pending queue
Related Classes: AutoPruneStrategy, ChainNode, TreeNode, TreeBuildingStrategy, BaseNode
Input: chain - ordered list of parsed ChainNodes.
Output: TreeNode root of the reconstructed document outline.
Pre-condition: chain is not null; if it is empty, the synthetic root is still produced.
Post-condition: The returned tree has root title "ROOT"; immediate nodes are attached, and non-immediate nodes are either attached as sibling groups or merged into content according to the auto-prune rules.

AutoPruneStrategy::addNodeAndUpdateBranch
Summary:
Attaches an immediate valid ChainNode to the nearest ancestor in currentBranch and updates the current branch so that it ends at the newly attached TreeNode.
Algorithm:
1. Create a TreeNode from the ChainNode using createTreeNode.
2. While currentBranch is not empty and the last node in currentBranch is not a direct parent of the new node, remove the last node.
3. If currentBranch is empty, the node cannot be attached (invalid for this operation).
4. Let parent = currentBranch.last; call parent.addChild(newNode).
5. Append newNode to currentBranch, so the branch represents the path from root to the new node.
Related Features: createTreeNode, currentBranch, TreeNode.parent, TreeNode.children, addChild
Related Classes: AutoPruneStrategy, ChainNode, TreeNode
Input: node - the ChainNode to attach; currentBranch - mutable list of TreeNodes representing the current root-to-leaf branch.
Output: None; currentBranch is updated as a side effect.
Pre-condition: node.levelSeq is an immediate valid next node after the current branch; currentBranch is non-empty and contains the synthetic root.
Post-condition: The new TreeNode is attached as a child of the nearest suitable ancestor, and currentBranch ends with that new TreeNode.

AutoPruneStrategy::isAllNotImmNodesSiblings
Summary:
Checks and applies the required auto-prune decision when the pending queue reaches three nodes. If all pending nodes form one immediate sibling sequence, the queue is left unchanged for the caller to attach. If they do not, the oldest pending node is removed and merged into the current node's content.
Algorithm:
1. If queue is empty, return.
2. Let firstSeq = queue.getFirst().levelSeq.
3. If firstSeq is empty, merge oldest into current content and return.
4. Let prefix = getPrefix(firstSeq).
5. Let expected = getLastLevel(firstSeq).
6. For each node in queue:
     seq = node.levelSeq
     if getPrefix(seq) != prefix or getLastLevel(seq) != expected:
         remove the oldest node from queue and merge it into current content.
         return
     expected = expected + 1
7. If the loop completes, all nodes are an immediate sibling sequence; leave the queue unchanged.
Related Features: getPrefix, getLastLevel, pending queue, current node content, concatNode
Related Classes: AutoPruneStrategy, ChainNode, TreeBuildingStrategy
Input: queue - Deque of pending ChainNodes that were not immediate next nodes.
Output: None; as a side effect, the oldest node may be removed and merged into content, or the queue may be left unchanged.
Pre-condition: queue is not null.
Post-condition: If all nodes are immediate siblings, queue remains intact for attachment. Otherwise, the oldest node is merged into current content and removed from the queue.

AutoPruneStrategy::createTreeNode
Summary:
Converts a ChainNode into a TreeNode, copying the title, level sequence, level text, and content, and initializing an empty children list and null parent.
Algorithm:
1. Create a new TreeNode.
2. Set tn.title = chainnode.title.
3. Set tn.levelSeq = new ArrayList(chainnode.levelSeq).
4. Set tn.levelText = chainnode.levelText.
5. Set tn.content = chainnode.content.
6. Set tn.parent = null.
7. Initialize tn.children as an empty list.
8. Return tn.
Related Features: ChainNode.title, ChainNode.levelSeq, ChainNode.levelText, ChainNode.content
Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeNode
Input: chainnode - ChainNode whose data is to be copied.
Output: New TreeNode instance.
Pre-condition: chainnode is not null; chainnode.levelSeq is not null.
Post-condition: The new TreeNode has the same heading information as the ChainNode and no children.

```plantuml
    addNodeAndUpdateBranch(node : ChainNode, currentBranch : List<TreeNode>) : void
```

# Operation Specifications
AutoPruneStrategy::addNodeToTree
Summary:
Lower-level helper that creates a TreeNode from a ChainNode, attaches it to the correct ancestor in currentBranch, and updates the current-node reference. It does not automatically append the new node to currentBranch; the caller does that after the branch has been trimmed.
Algorithm:
1. tn = createTreeNode(node)
2. While currentBranch is not empty and not isChild(currentBranch.last.levelSeq, node.levelSeq):
     currentBranch.removeLast()
3. If currentBranch is empty, reject the attachment.
4. parent = currentBranch.last
5. parent.addChild(tn)
6. Set currentNodeRef.value = tn
Related Features: createTreeNode, isChild, currentBranch, TreeNode.addChild
Related Classes: AutoPruneStrategy, ChainNode, TreeNode, TreeBuildingStrategy
Input: node - ChainNode to attach; currentBranch - mutable branch list for finding the parent; currentNodeRef - a mutable reference holder for the newly created current TreeNode.
Output: None; currentBranch and currentNodeRef are updated as side effects.
Pre-condition: node must have an ancestor represented in currentBranch; currentNodeRef is a mutable holder that can receive the new node.
Post-condition: node is linked into the tree under the nearest ancestor, and currentNodeRef refers to the newly added TreeNode.

AutoPruneStrategy::buildTree
Summary:
Builds a tree from the parsed chain using the auto-prune strategy, maintaining the latest valid branch and a pending queue for non-immediate nodes.
Algorithm:
1. Prepare a synthetic root TreeNode with levelSeq=[], title="ROOT", levelText="", content="".
   If the chain starts with a synthetic root ChainNode, use that node as the root and skip it.
2. currentBranch = [root]; current = root; pending = new Deque().
3. For each ChainNode cn in the remaining chain:
   a. If isImmNext(currentBranch.last.levelSeq, cn.levelSeq):
      - Merge every pending node into current.content in arrival order using concatNode.
      - Call addNodeAndUpdateBranch(cn, currentBranch).
      - current = currentBranch.last.
   b. Else:
      - Add cn to pending.
      - If pending.size() >= 3:
         oldSize = pending.size();
         isAllNotImmNodesSiblings(pending);
         if pending.size() == oldSize:
            // All pending nodes are an immediate sibling sequence; attach them in order.
            while pending not empty:
               addNodeAndUpdateBranch(pending.pollFirst(), currentBranch)
            current = currentBranch.last
         else:
            // The oldest pending node was already merged into current.content.
4. After the loop, merge all remaining pending nodes into current.content in arrival order.
5. Return root.
Related Features: isImmNext, addNodeAndUpdateBranch, isAllNotImmNodesSiblings, concatNode, createTreeNode, currentBranch, pending queue
Related Classes: AutoPruneStrategy, ChainNode, TreeNode, TreeBuildingStrategy, BaseNode
Input: chain - ordered list of parsed ChainNodes.
Output: TreeNode root of the reconstructed document outline.
Pre-condition: chain is not null; if it is empty, the synthetic root is still produced.
Post-condition: The returned tree has root title "ROOT"; immediate nodes are attached, and non-immediate nodes are either attached as sibling groups or merged into content according to the auto-prune rules.

AutoPruneStrategy::addNodeAndUpdateBranch
Summary:
Attaches an immediate valid ChainNode to the nearest ancestor in currentBranch and updates the current branch so that it ends at the newly attached TreeNode.
Algorithm:
1. Create a TreeNode from the ChainNode using createTreeNode.
2. While currentBranch is not empty and the last node in currentBranch is not a direct parent of the new node, remove the last node.
3. If currentBranch is empty, the node cannot be attached (invalid for this operation).
4. Let parent = currentBranch.last; call parent.addChild(newNode).
5. Append newNode to currentBranch, so the branch represents the path from root to the new node.
Related Features: createTreeNode, currentBranch, TreeNode.parent, TreeNode.children, addChild
Related Classes: AutoPruneStrategy, ChainNode, TreeNode
Input: node - the ChainNode to attach; currentBranch - mutable list of TreeNodes representing the current root-to-leaf branch.
Output: None; currentBranch is updated as a side effect.
Pre-condition: node.levelSeq is an immediate valid next node after the current branch; currentBranch is non-empty and contains the synthetic root.
Post-condition: The new TreeNode is attached as a child of the nearest suitable ancestor, and currentBranch ends with that new TreeNode.

AutoPruneStrategy::isAllNotImmNodesSiblings
Summary:
Checks and applies the required auto-prune decision when the pending queue reaches three nodes. If all pending nodes form one immediate sibling sequence, the queue is left unchanged for the caller to attach. If they do not, the oldest pending node is removed and merged into the current node's content.
Algorithm:
1. If queue is empty, return.
2. Let firstSeq = queue.getFirst().levelSeq.
3. If firstSeq is empty, merge oldest into current content and return.
4. Let prefix = getPrefix(firstSeq).
5. Let expected = getLastLevel(firstSeq).
6. For each node in queue:
     seq = node.levelSeq
     if getPrefix(seq) != prefix or getLastLevel(seq) != expected:
         remove the oldest node from queue and merge it into current content.
         return
     expected = expected + 1
7. If the loop completes, all nodes are an immediate sibling sequence; leave the queue unchanged.
Related Features: getPrefix, getLastLevel, pending queue, current node content, concatNode
Related Classes: AutoPruneStrategy, ChainNode, TreeBuildingStrategy
Input: queue - Deque of pending ChainNodes that were not immediate next nodes.
Output: None; as a side effect, the oldest node may be removed and merged into content, or the queue may be left unchanged.
Pre-condition: queue is not null.
Post-condition: If all nodes are immediate siblings, queue remains intact for attachment. Otherwise, the oldest node is merged into current content and removed from the queue.

AutoPruneStrategy::createTreeNode
Summary:
Converts a ChainNode into a TreeNode, copying the title, level sequence, level text, and content, and initializing an empty children list and null parent.
Algorithm:
1. Create a new TreeNode.
2. Set tn.title = chainnode.title.
3. Set tn.levelSeq = new ArrayList(chainnode.levelSeq).
4. Set tn.levelText = chainnode.levelText.
5. Set tn.content = chainnode.content.
6. Set tn.parent = null.
7. Initialize tn.children as an empty list.
8. Return tn.
Related Features: ChainNode.title, ChainNode.levelSeq, ChainNode.levelText, ChainNode.content
Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeNode
Input: chainnode - ChainNode whose data is to be copied.
Output: New TreeNode instance.
Pre-condition: chainnode is not null; chainnode.levelSeq is not null.
Post-condition: The new TreeNode has the same heading information as the ChainNode and no children.

```java
   * Parses an entire structured text into an ordered list of ChainNodes. Heading lines become

   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary:
   * Tries each registered LevelPattern in order until a valid heading pattern is found.
   * If a pattern matches and numeric conversion succeeds, returns a ChainNode representing
   * the heading; otherwise returns null. Invalid numeric text does not create a valid heading.
   * Algorithm:
   * 1. For each pattern p in patterns, with index i:
   *    a. Get matcher = p.getRegex().matcher(line).
   *    b. If no anchored match, continue to the next pattern.
   *    c. Extract matchedText from the capturing group that holds the numbering text.
   *    d. Convert matchedText via p.convertMatchedText(matchedText).
   *    e. If conversion fails or yields null/empty levelSeq, continue to the next pattern.
   *    f. If levelSeq.size() < p.minLevel or levelSeq.size() > p.maxLevel, continue.
   *    g. Determine title = line substring after the matched heading marker and separator,
   *       trimmed of leading/trailing whitespace.
   *    h. Return createChainNode(levelSeq, title, "", matchedText, i).
   * 2. If no pattern succeeds, return null.
   * Related Features: patterns, createChainNode, LevelPattern.getRegex, LevelPattern.convertMatchedText, LevelPattern.separator, LevelPattern.minLevel, LevelPattern.maxLevel

   * Output: ChainNode if the line is a heading; null otherwise.
   * Pre-condition: line is not null.
   * Post-condition: The first valid pattern determines the level sequence and patternPriority;

   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
```
   * @generated NOT

  public ChainNode detectLevel(final String line)
  {
    for (int i = 0; i < getPatterns().size(); i++)
    {
      LevelPattern p = getPatterns().get(i);
      Matcher matcher = p.getRegex().matcher(line);
      if (!matcher.lookingAt())
      {
        continue;
      }
      String matchedText = matcher.group(1);
      EList<Integer> levelSeq = p.convertMatchedText(matchedText);
      if (levelSeq == null || levelSeq.isEmpty())
      {
        continue;
      }
      if (levelSeq.size() < p.getMinLevel() || levelSeq.size() > p.getMaxLevel())
      {
        continue;
      }
      String title = line.substring(matcher.end()).trim();
      return createChainNode(levelSeq, title, "", matchedText, i);
    }
    return null;

    TreeNode root = ArborparserFactory.eINSTANCE.createTreeNode();
    root.setTitle("ROOT");

    Deque<TreeNode> stack = new ArrayDeque<TreeNode>();
    stack.addLast(root);

    for (ChainNode cn : chain)
    {
      if (stack.isEmpty() || !isImmNext(stack.getLast().getLevelSeq(), cn.getLevelSeq()))
      {
        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Invalid chain: does not follow the exact immediate level-sequence relation");
      }

      while (!isChild(stack.getLast().getLevelSeq(), cn.getLevelSeq()))
      {
        stack.removeLast();
      }

      TreeNode tn = createTreeNode(cn);
      stack.getLast().addChild(tn);
      stack.addLast(tn);
    }

    return root;
  }

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary:
   * Tests whether childSeq is a direct child sequence of parentSeq, i.e., childSeq has exactly one more level than parentSeq and parentSeq is its prefix.
   * Algorithm:
   * 1. If parentSeq or childSeq is null, return false.
   * 2. If childSeq.size() != parentSeq.size() + 1, return false.
   * 3. Return childSeq.subList(0, parentSeq.size()).equals(parentSeq).
   * Related Features: None
   * Related Classes: None
   * Input: parentSeq - base level sequence; childSeq - candidate child level sequence.
   * Output: boolean true if childSeq extends parentSeq by one element; false otherwise.
   * Pre-condition: parentSeq and childSeq are non-null.
   * Post-condition: Returns true only when the child relation holds.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model parentSeqMany="true" childSeqMany="true"
   *        annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public boolean isChild(final EList<Integer> parentSeq, final EList<Integer> childSeq)
  {
    if (parentSeq == null || childSeq == null)
    {
      return false;
    }

    if (childSeq.size() != parentSeq.size() + 1)
    {
      return false;
    }

    return childSeq.subList(0, parentSeq.size()).equals(parentSeq);
  }

```java
   * Summary:
   * Builds a tree from the parsed chain using the auto-prune strategy, maintaining the latest valid branch and a pending queue for non-immediate nodes.
   * Algorithm:
   * 1. Prepare a synthetic root TreeNode with levelSeq=[], title="ROOT", levelText="", content="".
   *    If the chain starts with a synthetic root ChainNode, use that node as the root and skip it.
   * 2. currentBranch = [root]; current = root; pending = new Deque().
   * 3. For each ChainNode cn in the remaining chain:

   *             while pending not empty:
   *                addNodeAndUpdateBranch(pending.pollFirst(), currentBranch)
   *             current = currentBranch.last
   *          else:
   *             // The oldest pending node was already merged into current.content.
   * 4. After the loop, merge all remaining pending nodes into current.content in arrival order.
   * 5. Return root.
   * Related Features: isImmNext, addNodeAndUpdateBranch, isAllNotImmNodesSiblings, concatNode, createTreeNode, currentBranch, pending queue
```
